records.name: First Presbyterian Church Casserole Volunteers
records.summary: A Center City church that gathers volunteers after Sunday worship to assemble casseroles for the University City Hospitality Coalition's free meals. Each session is listed as about 45 minutes and ends with time to visit.
records.what_you_do: Assemble 30 to 40 casseroles together in Old Buttonwood Hall, then stay to visit with the other volunteers.

schedule.text: Sessions are held on some Sundays and listed one at a time on the church's event pages, so check the date before you come. The church's regular Sunday services are at 9 am and 11 am.

locations.label: Old Buttonwood Hall, inside the church

cost.text: The event pages do not mention any cost to volunteers.

first_step.how: Email Laura Colee at laura.colee@fpcphila.org to sign up for the next casserole session.
first_step.basis: The event pages ask volunteers to contact a named person first, and the work is team based and social. They do not say newcomers are welcome or that walk-ins are fine.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each session is listed as about 45 minutes. Volunteers work together in Old Buttonwood Hall to assemble 30 to 40 casseroles, then stay to visit. The pages do not say whether any experience is needed.
first_visit_tips: Email Laura Colee ahead of time, since sign up is needed.
Old Buttonwood Hall is inside the church at 201 South 21st Street, at Walnut Street.
The event pages give no parking or transit notes, so plan your trip before you go.

records.notes: The June and August sessions were listed as following a 10 am combined service, but the church home page now shows 9 am and 11 am services, so the session time may differ; confirm with the contact. The Sunday Volunteers page (ushers and fellowship helpers) is a separate route and is not the casserole sign up. The August event page states no walk-in policy. The mission page lists University City Hospitality Coalition and about 25 other partners; they are in leads_only, and the international partners were left out as not Philadelphia groups.

records.name: Fisher Park Community Alliance
records.summary: The volunteer group that has looked after Fisher Park in Olney, a hilly, wooded park of about 23 acres, since the 1980s. The most recent activity we could date is from 2018, so check with the city before you plan to join.
records.what_you_do: In 2018 the group ran park cleanups, tree plantings, a community garden and neighborhood events such as movie nights. We could not confirm that this continues.

first_step.how: Ask Philadelphia Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) to connect you with this Friends group.
first_step.basis: A 2018 article says new families are welcome, but we found no current way to sign up, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Tier 1 marked this active from the city listing, which is a listing and not dated activity. The only dated evidence found is a May 2018 Fairmount Park Conservancy article, so status is dormant. A search also turned up a 2009 profile saying the group was doing less than before; it was not fetched. The city list says 572 W Spencer St while the 2018 article says 600 W Spencer Ave; the city address was kept. The Facebook page is a leads only source and was not read; the link moved from website to social. The pprstewardship email is carried from tier 1 and was not re-verified. Owner review: this group has no current public activity we could find, so the owner may want to decide whether to keep it published.

records.name: Fleisher Art Memorial
records.summary: An art center on Catharine Street with adult classes, youth art programs, a free Teen Lounge for teens, and community festivals. Tuition-free classes need a membership, and members get a discount on paid classes.
records.what_you_do: Take an adult or youth art class, drop in to the Teen Lounge on Tuesday and Wednesday afternoons during the school year, or join as a member to get into tuition-free classes and a discount on paid ones.

schedule.text: Adult and youth classes run in terms. During term, the front desk is open Monday to Thursday 9 am to 9:30 pm, Friday 9 am to 8 pm, and Saturday 9 am to 3:30 pm. The Teen Lounge meets Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 4 to 6 pm during the school year.

cost.text: Membership is $65 a year for adults, $50 for seniors 65 and older, and $120 for a household of up to four adults and children. Members get 10 percent off tuition-based classes. Tuition-based classes set tuition by length, studio fees vary by medium, and open studio drop in is $10 for students taking a class in that medium. Tuition assistance covers tuition only.

access.notes: The main building at 719 Catharine has an elevator, and a lift serves visitors who use mobility devices during open hours. Accessible parking is in the lot and in front of the school entrance on Catharine Street. The 709 Catharine building has no accessible restroom. Nearest SEPTA: the Route 47 bus stop at 8th and Christian Streets, about half a block away. For lift help, call the front desk at 215-922-3456 ext. 300.

first_step.how: Register for a class through the online class search, by phone at 215-922-3456 ext. 300, or at the front desk. Paid classes do not need a membership, but tuition-free classes do.
first_step.basis: Classes are open to the public with online, phone and desk sign up. Some tuition-free classes are labeled introductory, but most classes are not labeled by level.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each class meets on the dates in its listing, within a term. Tuition depends on class length, and studio and material fees depend on the medium. Tuition assistance covers tuition only, and the site notes that waiting lists form when classes fill.
first_visit_tips: Parking is limited. The student lot across from the main entrance is open only during programming hours, and paid and free city lots are nearby.
Bike racks are along Catharine Street and the lot fence.
If you need the lift, call the front desk first.

records.notes: The open studio drop in fee of $10 comes from the adult education page; the tier 1 source (home page) does not show it. Adult fall 2026 tuition assistance applications closed August 7, 2026. The Teen Lounge age range is not stated; the page asks teens to email cy@fleisher.org to confirm eligibility. Membership prices and benefits come from the membership page. Tier 1 said some classes need a membership, which the membership page confirms for tuition-free classes only.

records.name: Fletcher Street Urban Riding Club
records.summary: A nonprofit riding club on Fletcher Street in the Strawberry Mansion area of North Philadelphia. It serves young people from across the city, teaching them to ride and to care for horses.
records.what_you_do: Learn to ride, feed, groom and care for horses, and take part in club life such as classes, events and weekend rides to equine campgrounds for active members.

schedule.text: The pages we read do not list riding days or times. Ask through the member information request form.

cost.text: A 2025 news report said riding is free for kids and families. The club's own site asks for donations and does not state a fee.

first_step.how: Fill out the member information request form on the club's website. The club says it reviews each request and follows up within one week.
first_step.basis: The only way in is an application. The form asks for a parent or guardian and the child's details, approval is not guaranteed, and applicants under 18 meet by video with a parent or guardian and board members.
first_step.what_to_expect: The first step is an application, and applicants under 18 have a virtual meeting with a parent or guardian and board members before they join. Riders are placed by skill level, from beginner to advanced, and members also feed, groom and bond with the horses. The pages we read do not give session length or fees.
first_visit_tips: Send the member information request form first, since the club says approval is not guaranteed.
If you want to help with the barn instead, the site has a separate volunteer registration form.
While an application is pending, minors may come to the stables only with a parent or legal guardian.

records.notes: The cost and last sign of life come from the tier 1 CBS report, which was not re-read in this pass. The news page has no dated items from recent years (only an undated statement and a 2014 residency note). Riding days and times are not published on the pages read. The member form asks for a child's grade from 1 to 12, so the club serves children; no minimum age is stated. The form was read only and not submitted. Newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 because the form is an application with review. Dropped the tier 1 contact_name, which repeated the club name.

records.name: Fort Mifflin on the Delaware
records.summary: A historic fort on the Delaware River in southwest Philadelphia, run by a nonprofit. It hosts school and scout visits, guided tours, cannon and living history demonstrations, and candlelit ghost tours.
records.what_you_do: Visit the fort on an open day, take a tour, bring a school or scout group, or join as a member to support its historic programs and restoration.

schedule.text: Open to visitors Wednesday to Sunday, 10 am to 4 pm, from March 1 to December 15. Weekend tours run at 11 am and 2 pm, and a cannon demonstration is at 1 pm. From December 15 to March 1 the fort is open only for private events and appointments. School and group tours can be booked in advance, seven days a week.

locations.label: Fort Mifflin, at Fort Mifflin Road and Hog Island Road

cost.text: The 2025 admission prices were $16 for adults, $14 for seniors, $12 for veterans, and $10 for children 6 to 12. Children 5 and under and active duty military with ID are free. Some living history events cost extra. Membership, called Join Us, runs $35 to $275 a year and includes free general admission.

first_step.how: Come during open hours, Wednesday to Sunday from 10 am to 4 pm between March 1 and December 15, and join a weekend tour at 11 am or 2 pm.
first_step.basis: General admission needs no sign up, and the Join Us membership gives a clear way to join. The site does not describe any volunteer role.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit is a walk around a historic fort on the Delaware River, with a shaded riverfront picnic area and free parking. Weekend tours run at 11 am and 2 pm, and a cannon demonstration happens at 1 pm. Some living history events cost extra on top of admission.
first_visit_tips: Parking is free once you follow the signs into the fort.
The site does not describe wheelchair access, so call 856-831-5690 before you come.
Leashed pets are welcome on the grounds, though cannon and musket demonstrations may frighten some animals.

records.notes: No volunteer roles appear on the home, contact, plan your visit, join or events pages, so the tier 1 volunteer tags were replaced: walking_tours is the closest tag for guided tours, and the role is figure_out. The membership is called Join Us on the site, not Join The Fort. The events page lists Oct 3, Oct 9, Oct 24 and Dec 5 events without years, so no 2026 event is recorded. The dated facts are the 2025 admission prices and an office hours note for winter 2024/25 on the contact page, so status is probably_active with no month of last sign of life. The site gives no transit or wheelchair access details. Owner review: this is a visitor attraction run by a nonprofit with a membership and no volunteer or group role we could find; the owner may decide it fits not_a_group better than publish.

records.name: FPA Philadelphia Tri-State Area
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the Financial Planning Association, a professional group that brings together almost 500 local financial planners. It offers talks, networking and a mentorship program that pairs newer planners with experienced ones.
records.what_you_do: Attend talks and networking events, register for a holiday party, or ask about the mentorship program if you are a newer planner.

schedule.text: Events are scheduled one at a time, not on a set meeting schedule. The chapter's mentorship program meets monthly for six months.

cost.text: The chapter page does not list event prices for members or non-members, and the FPA membership page we read does not show dues.

first_step.how: Sign up for an upcoming chapter event through its registration link, or call chapter executive Kristin Beane at 508-320-1685 to ask about the mentorship program.
first_step.basis: Events are listed publicly with registration links, and the chapter runs a mentorship program for newer planners. The page does not say whether non-members can attend, and the mentorship details cover only the 2026 round.
first_step.what_to_expect: Chapter events are talks on financial planning topics and social evenings. The October 14, 2026 event is a one hour virtual talk on private markets, and the December 10, 2026 party includes food, drinks and networking; its location is still to be set. The mentorship pairs one newer planner with one experienced planner, with monthly meetings from March through August of the 2026 round.
first_visit_tips: The October 14 talk is virtual, so you can join from home.
The December party's location is still to be set, so check for an update before you plan your trip.

records.notes: The mentorship registration page on lp.constantcontactpages.com returned HTTP 403 and was not retried (see blocked), so mentorship facts come from the chapter page only. The chapter page names the 2026 round (virtual kickoff February 26, monthly meetings March to August), so ask the chapter about the next round. The February 25, 2027 Northeast Symposium is in New York and is not recorded as a local event. The chapter page lists no member or non-member event prices, and the FPA membership page shows no dues. The chapter email is obscured on the page, so only the phone is recorded.

records.name: Friends Fridge Philly
records.summary: A free community fridge on West Clearfield Street in the Allegheny West and Nicetown-Tioga area. Anyone can take food from it, and neighbors can leave food or sign up to help stock, cook, drive or clean it.
records.what_you_do: Take food you need, leave food you can spare, or sign up on the volunteer form to stock the fridge, make meals, drive food to and from it, or help with upkeep.

schedule.text: The fridge is open to anyone. The site does not list hours or how often the fridge is stocked.

first_step.how: Visit the fridge to take or leave food, or fill in the volunteer sign up form linked from the group's site to help out.
first_step.basis: The fridge is open to anyone with no sign up to visit, and volunteers join through a public form. The pages do not describe how long a shift runs.
first_step.what_to_expect: Visiting means walking up to the fridge to take food or leave food; the site describes no check in. Volunteers do stocking, meal prep (packing containers and making sandwiches), driving food to and from the fridge, and upkeep such as cleaning. The site does not say how long a shift runs.
first_visit_tips: The site does not list hours, so call 215.226.1276 before you go to ask when the fridge is stocked.
The location page gives the address only, with no transit or parking notes, so plan your trip before you go.

records.notes: The kind changed from network to program, since this is one fridge run with partners rather than a network of groups. The About page says St. James School and William Penn Charter School created it, and the partners page names St. James Welcome Table (Instagram only, no website shown) and an Instagram handle with no name. No hours, stocking schedule, food rules or dated items with years were found on the site. The CityCast source is carried from tier 1 and was not re-read in this pass. The Instagram link on the location page points to a generic address, so the handle link from the home page is kept.

notes: Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used (for a Fisher Park site of its own; it returned only 2009 to 2018 material). 30 WebFetch calls across 7 groups, none over 6 per group, no rate limiting seen. Fisher Park's Facebook link was not read (leads only). All 7 records have verdict publish. Changes from tier 1: (1) Fisher Park status moved from active to dormant, because the newest dated activity found is May 2018 and the city listing is not dated activity; (2) Friends Fridge kind changed from network to program; (3) Fletcher Street newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 because the member form is an application with review; (4) Fort Mifflin volunteer tags replaced with walking_tours and figure_out, since no volunteer roles appear on its site, and its membership is called Join Us; (5) First Presbyterian session time may differ from the 10 am service in the event pages, since the church home page lists 9 am and 11 am. Owner review requested: Fisher Park (dormant, no current contact beyond the city) and Fort Mifflin (a visitor attraction with a membership, which may fit not_a_group better). Leads include the church and Friends Fridge partners named on their own sites; none of the leads with a known website was fetched, because the only websites named were partner pages or Instagram handles.
